title: STEWARD-14 — accepted retention decisions for the fourteen categories CUT-1 refused

authority.northern_star_rule: R19 — retention is a number of years with a basis; a disposal date must be calculable

basis_note: The R19 basis stays where it already lives: specs/governance-library/taxonomy.json `retention_rule`. This file records only the steward's reading of that prose — taxonomy_id, years, anchor and a short rationale. No prose is copied here, and none of it was edited to make these decisions fit (F-7 §4: one home per fact).
principle: Where the prose names more than one period, the longest leg governs the whole category. One category-level integer cannot hold two, and keeping a record longer than its rule requires is recoverable; destroying it early is not.
A period stated in months rounds UP to the next whole year, because R19 makes retention a count of years.

Where the prose says the current issue is kept ('Current …', 'Register current', 'Certificates current'), the anchor is `supersede`, so a live document has no disposal date at all and the clock starts the day it leaves the live set. Anchoring those at `issue` is what made a document disposable the day it stopped being current.

A per-document extension the register cannot evaluate ('longer if incident-related', 'to age 21 if a minor', 'if contractual') is NOT a category default. It stays a steward action on the individual document, and the category carries the period that applies without it.

decisions.rationale: Longest leg (exposure-monitoring linked records, 40 years) governs the whole category; supersede anchor honours the 'Current' leg, so a live COSHH assessment has no disposal date.

The register does not record whether a method statement is contractual, so the longer conditional leg (contract life + 6 years) governs unconditionally. Supersede anchor preserves the 'Current +' reading.

Base period 3 years from issue. 'Longer if incident-related' is a per-permit extension a steward applies to the document; it cannot be a category default because the register does not know which permits are incident-related.
'Completed' describes the only record type this category holds, so the colon introduces a scope word rather than a second period. 3 years from issue.
Longest leg (investigations, 6 years) governs the whole category; '3 years minimum' is a floor, not a ceiling, and the age-21 extension for a minor stays a per-document steward action.
'Health records' is the whole content of this category, so the colon is a scope word, not a second period. 40 years from issue.

3 years anchored on supersede satisfies both legs with one rule: a live PEEP has no disposal date ('PEEPs: current'), a superseded drill record keeps 3 years. 'restricted' is an access statement and is already carried by default_access.
Longest leg (exposure records, 40 years) governs the whole category; supersede anchor honours 'Register current'.

Longest leg (EL certificates, 40 years) governs the whole category, and 'recommended' is read as required rather than optional. Issue anchor: an insurance certificate's clock starts on the day it is issued, and it is never superseded in place.
15 months rounded up to the next whole year. 2 years from issue is longer than the prose requires and never shorter; a 1-year rounding would have been.

Longest leg (working time records, 2 years) governs the whole category, which also covers the 12-month tachograph leg. The category is seeded inactive — Plantexpand runs no HGVs under an O-licence — so this governs rows already filed, not new ones.
Longest leg (reports, 6 years) with a supersede anchor, which also satisfies 'Certificates current' — a live certificate has no disposal date.
Longest leg (consignment notes, 3 years) governs the whole category, which also covers the 2-year transfer-note leg.
Longest leg (incidents, 6 years) with a supersede anchor, honouring 'Register current'.
